subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and requested details
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finovate.ai>
Cc: Greg Li <greg.li@finovate.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and requested details

Hi Anita / Greg,

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation and excited about the potential fit between Finovate AI and Redwood Dedicated. As promised, next steps for sizing the Dedicated capacity are the list of workloads/targets below. If you can reply with the values (or a ballpark) we can produce an initial sizing and a committed quote.

Requested items: 
- TPS target (inference requests per second) during peak sustained windows (e.g., 9–11am) and expected burst TPS.
- Typical concurrency per session (how many simultaneous user sessions calling the model) and average requests per session.
- Average prompt length and average generated tokens per response (token mix: prompt tokens vs generated tokens). If unknown, a sample 10–20 call traces is extremely helpful.
- Preferred model families (we discussed Llama 2–style open models and also an option to use a finetuned encoder-decoder). Do you expect to run heavier LLMs (e.g., 30B+) or smaller 7B/13B variants?
- Compliance/networking: do you need Private (VPC) deployment or is Dedicated with private tenancy enough? Any specific region constraints?
- Target latency SLO (p95 token/response latency) and what % of traffic needs sub-300ms responses vs. more relaxed 

Attached: finovate-sizing-sheet-v1.xlsx — fill any sections you can. I’ll also loop Marissa (Solutions) to validate concurrency and ingestion patterns.

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill the sizing sheet and return it (or drop sample traces to the Drive link).
2) Marissa and I will produce a recommended GPU pool (type + node count) and a draft committed quote.
3) 30-min follow-up next week to review.

If easier, a one-line reply with the TPS/concurrency and token averages is enough to get started.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

--
Attachment: finovate-sizing-sheet-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet - 48KB)
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finovate.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Greg Li <greg.li@finovate.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and requested details

Hi Rafael,

Thanks — please see answers inline. I also attached a quick export of 24h traffic and a short sample of requests.

- TPS target: peak sustained ~45 TPS, with bursts up to ~120 TPS for short periods (30–60s). Typical sustained window is 09:00–11:00 PT.
- Concurrency: we expect ~140 concurrent sessions during peak. Each session makes ~1.5 calls/min on average (interactive chat behavior).
- Token mix: average prompt tokens ~220, average generation ~180. So ~400 tokens total per request. We have a mix of short (50–100 tokens) and long (800+ tokens) tail requests — ~12% of calls are long-form summarization at ~1,200 generated tokens.
- Models: plan to use a mix — baseline 13B open model for most traffic and occasional 33B for complex summarization jobs. We are open to quantized variants if you recommend.
- Deployment: Dedicated with private tenancy is preferred — we do not need fully private VPC for now but may in the future. Region: us-west.
- Latency SLO: target p95 end-to-end <600ms for the 13B baseline; long-form jobs have a relaxed SLO ~3–4s.

Attached: finovate-24h-traces.csv, sample-calls.json (10 traces). Let me know if you need more.

Cheers,
Anita Shah
Head of ML Product | Finovate AI
anita.shah@finovate.ai

--
Attachments: finovate-24h-traces.csv (CSV - 120KB); sample-calls.json (JSON - 12KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@finovate.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and requested details

Rafael — quick internal note (copying Anita so they see our plan):

Thanks Anita, that data is very helpful. Based on the initial numbers I’m going to propose the following glide-path for a Dedicated pool tuned for latency and cost:

- Baseline traffic (13B): target 45 sustained TPS -> recommend 8 nodes of A100-80GB (or equivalent G72 in newer infra) with continuous batching and KV cache enabled. This should hit your p95 <600ms for 13B for average token mixes.
- Burst headroom: autoscaling to add 4 extra nodes for short bursts up to 120 TPS (scale-up target ~90s).
- Long-form jobs (33B): schedule to a separate queued pool (2 nodes of H100-style or 2x larger memory nodes) for the 12% long tail; allow async job execution with higher latency SLO.
- Concurrency: 140 concurrent sessions maps to ~18 concurrent requests/node assuming the baseline pool above; we’ll validate during a short load run.

Questions for sizing validation:
1) Can you confirm percent of traffic that requires generation >800 tokens? Anita indicated ~12% long-form.
2) Are there any strict request-level encryption/KMS requirements beyond our standard Dedicated offering?

I’ll build a quick cost estimate and a committed quote for Rafael to attach. Rafael — do you want me to include a private VPC option as an alternate line item?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

1) Marissa will finalize the node recommendation and cost estimate (including an optional Private VPC line). Expect the draft quote by EOD Wed (14 Jul).
2) We’ll provision a small proof-of-load run (non-prod) to validate latency assumptions — would you be available for a 60-min test window next Tue 21 July? We’ll coordinate exact times once the pool is provisioned.
3) I’ll open a HubSpot opportunity and share the DocuSign link for a 3-month evaluation commitment (we can include conversion credits if you choose a 12-month committed plan).

If anything changes on the traffic side or you want us to run a quick simulation with different quantization profiles, let me know and Marissa can spin that up.
